question: Should AI Council implement the corrected usefulness-measurement MVP now?
rationale: Forecast calibration alone cannot measure whether a seat adds a novel useful finding.
The existing append-only ledger and scoring core provide a tested base for additive evidence capture.
The Claude review reduced the original plan to a throughput-bounded capture MVP.
knownConsiderations: The live council currently has four standing seats and no resolved strict council outcomes.
Historical reconstructed baselines cannot support prospective novelty claims.
Per-cell novelty and confidently-wrong adjudication was noisy.
Recent councils are serially dependent within a small number of decision families.
The evidence tree currently lacks a project-owned backup mechanism.
Adding seats before finding capture would generate more unscoreable output.
scope: Tier-1 per-seat input and output artifact references and digests
explicit voting, shadow, and control seat roles
atomic findings with forced dispositions and co-occurrence groups
outOfScope: hidden reasoning or complete tool-output capture
mindChangers: A reviewer demonstrates that the additive schema cannot preserve strict validation of existing rows.
The artifact design requires storing secrets, hidden reasoning, or irrelevant raw tool output.
The workflow cannot keep expected human handling time at or below three minutes per council.
The proposed metrics allow intervention-sensitive outcomes into headline Brier scores.
Parallel implementation cannot be integrated without weakening append-only or fail-closed behavior.
implementationGate: All unit and integration tests pass; copied-live rehearsal changes no live evidence; final council has no BLOCK.
rolloutGate: Capture-only soak; no seat performance claims until the statistical gate is separately frozen.
